title: Normandy: beyond the landing
hook: After D-Day, what kept the armies supplied?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: The landing was the start of a supply problem.

claims.text: 6 Jun: Landings. Allied forces land on Normandy beaches.
claims.source: https://www.nationalww2museum.org/war/articles/over-shore-logistics-d-day — Curatola, June 2025: Cherbourg, Mulberries, storm and beach logistics; USHMM D-Day for June 6; https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/timeline-event/holocaust/1942-1945/d-day — June 6, 1944 landings

claims.text: 16 Jun: Artificial harbors. Mulberries begin unloading supplies.
claims.source: https://www.nationalww2museum.org/war/articles/over-shore-logistics-d-day — Curatola, June 2025: Cherbourg, Mulberries, storm and beach logistics; USHMM D-Day for June 6; https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/timeline-event/holocaust/1942-1945/d-day — June 6, 1944 landings

claims.text: 19–21 Jun: Storm. A storm damages the American harbor.
claims.source: https://www.nationalww2museum.org/war/articles/over-shore-logistics-d-day — Curatola, June 2025: Cherbourg, Mulberries, storm and beach logistics; USHMM D-Day for June 6; https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/timeline-event/holocaust/1942-1945/d-day — June 6, 1944 landings

claims.text: Late Jun: Beaches endure. Beach supply continues; Cherbourg remains unusable.
claims.source: https://www.nationalww2museum.org/war/articles/over-shore-logistics-d-day — Curatola, June 2025: Cherbourg, Mulberries, storm and beach logistics; USHMM D-Day for June 6; https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/timeline-event/holocaust/1942-1945/d-day — June 6, 1944 landings

claims.text: The landing was the start of a supply problem. Artificial harbors helped, but the June storm damaged the American Mulberry. Beaches continued handling supplies while Cherbourg’s damaged port could not yet serve the armies. A captured port was not automatically a usable one.
claims.source: https://www.nationalww2museum.org/war/articles/over-shore-logistics-d-day — Curatola, June 2025: Cherbourg, Mulberries, storm and beach logistics; USHMM D-Day for June 6; https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/timeline-event/holocaust/1942-1945/d-day — June 6, 1944 landings

recall.question: Which supply route still mattered at the end of June?
recall.why: The landing was the start of a supply problem. Artificial harbors helped, but the June storm damaged the American Mulberry. Beaches continued handling supplies while Cherbourg’s damaged port could not yet serve the armies. A captured port was not automatically a usable one.
